messages.subject: multispecies modeling error and observation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to use wallace to model multiple species, and I got the following error:

Warning: Error in ENMeval : : ENMevaluate: Removal of cell duplicates caused one or more partition groups to be missing. Please make sure all partition groups are represented by at least one non-duplicate occurrence record.
2: shine : : runApp
1: run_wallace

I am using jacknife k=n and I have previously thin my occurrences to 5km plus using the 5km cell resolution and wallace said before it had removed duplicate cells.

After doing this, the screen is gray and it does not continue. Any suggestions?

As an observation, when you are using multiplespecies, and you delimit the background points, if you use one amount it will use it for all of the species (if you select batch). Wouldn't it be better to select batch, and you get a message that it tells you how much background points can be generated for all of the species and let you decide if you want that quantity or modify it rather than doing it one by one (making the batch function not useful)?

Cheers,
Oscar

We're working on fixing this issue. We've run into it before when a locality falls on or near the edge of a raster pixel and they aren't removed by Wallace but are getting removed during partitioning. In the meantime, the workaround is as Dakota mentioned- using another partitioning method. I'll report back when I hear more from the team on this.

-Bethany

Dear all,
I would like to ask a question about the referees’ comments. I thinned my occurrence records 5-km radius buffer around each occurrence record using the spThin. But I used 30 arcsec - 1 km resolution layers as predictors. He/she asks "If the variables are at 1 km, why thinning at 5 km?" should I consider predictor resolution when thinning my records? Is there any thumb of rule about this subject? Any suggestion would be appreciated. Best greets, Kerim

messages.subject: Re: should I consider predictor resolution when thinning my records
messages.subject_clean: should I consider predictor resolution when thinning my records
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kerim,
Yes, you can consider the resolution of predictors when thinning. You can also consider the species biology, such as its dispersal or home range. Spatial thinning aims at reducing errors from sampling bias. More information on thinning can be found here- https://doi.org/10.1111/ecog.01132, the Aiello-Lammens et al. paper on the spThin R-package and spatial thinning for ecological niche modeling.
-Bethany

messages.subject: Wallace 1.9.3-6 "Error in addLegend unused arguments" with Process Occs and Partition Occs --
messages.subject_clean: Wallace 1.9.3-6 "Error in addLegend unused arguments" with Process Occs and Partition Occs --
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm using Wallace to work on ENM with a summer intern.  We found an error when Wallace tries to "addLegend" to Proccess Occs and Partition Occs outputs:

In "Proccess Occs"  when I click "Spatial Thin" it calculates, but does not display the results, Wallace crashes with a gray screen and I get this error in the console:

Warning: Error in addLegend: unused arguments (colors = c("red", "blue"), title = "Occ Records", labels = c("retained", "removed"), opacity = 1)

In "Partition Occs"  when I select any option and then click "Partition" it calculates but does not display the results, Wallace crashes with a gray screen and I get a similar error in the console:

Warning: Error in addLegend: unused arguments (colors = newColors, title = "Partition Groups", labels = sort(unique(occsGrp)), opacity = 1)

As these are all proper arguments ts to "leaflet::addLegend" perhaps this function is not receiving the map data from which to operate?  Looking over the GitHub code for poccs_thinOccs.R <https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace/blob/5299abb8dbea5b4cdc262de110f39c99b230aeac/inst/shiny/modules/poccs_thinOccs.R> & part_spat.R <https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace/blob/5299abb8dbea5b4cdc262de110f39c99b230aeac/inst/shiny/modules/part_spat.R> doesn't reveal anything obvious.

I was able to replicate this behavior with our custom GBIF dataset as well as generic data loaded from GBIF (1000 observations from Larus occidentalis) and got the exact same errors.

Do you have any suggestions for how to fix this error in the "addLegend" portion of the Shiny app?

For relevant session information see below.

Thanks for making such a great app!

All the best,

Durrell

Hi,

Thanks, Bethany, your email prompted me to try to replicate your experience by starting again from a clean slate and installing all the supporting packages one more time. I'm almost embarrassed to say that the two modules I was having difficulty with WORKED!

I will keep an eye out when I help others use wallace but it looks like there was a supporting package glitch, now that all those are reinstalled everything is great.

Thanks for the excellent Shiny app.

Best,

Durrell
